newsitem.title: UK: Azlan rights issue flops, Warburg to sell.
newsitem.headline: Azlan rights issue flops, Warburg to sell.

text.p: A rights issue by British information technology training and support firm Azlan Plc failed to win interest from shareholders and left advisers SBC Warburg attempting to sell about a quarter of the new shares which it acquired in its capacity as main underwriter.

The company said on Monday its three-for-10 issue, which had been priced at 620 pence per share, would have offered a maximum of 8.18 million new shares but only 45,774 were taken up by existing shareholders.
In a statement it added that Warburg intended to operate a pool of buyers and sellers of the shares among sub-underwriters, and said it would, subject to price, be a seller itself.
The bank had been left with 2.22 million Azlan shares, bought at the full offer price, which in total represented about 6.26 percent of the group's enlarged share capital.

Later, the Evening Standard newspaper reported that Warburg's pool succeeded in making some sales at a price of 550 pence during the day, at a discount to Azlan's prevailing market share price of between 567.5 pence and 570 pence.
Azlan had said it wanted the rights issue to riase funds for a planned 30 million stg purchase of Dutch company Akam BV.
